skill.name: email-campaign-specialist
skill.description: Plan, write, review, and measure broadcast email campaigns and newsletters on any email platform. Use for campaign briefs, audience selection, subject lines, email copy, launch QA, and campaign experiments; not cold-outreach prospecting or detailed automation engineering.
skill.summary: Create broadcast campaign briefs, email drafts, launch reviews, and measurement plans using your existing email platform.
skill.author: email-marketing-skills-hub

content.value_statement: Email campaigns need clear audiences, accurate copy, and reliable launch checks. This skill structures briefs, drafts messages, and guides measurement using your existing platform.
actual_capabilities: Build campaign briefs covering goals, audience eligibility, exclusions, offers, schedules, ownership, and measurement windows.
Draft subject lines, preheaders, body copy, primary calls to action, and requested plain-text equivalents.
Define audience logic while preserving consent scope, preferences, suppression lists, and deduplication requirements.
Review launch dependencies, personalization fallbacks, links, sender settings, scheduling details, and authorization requirements.
Plan campaign experiments and interpret click, conversion, revenue, unsubscribe, and delivery metrics with explicit denominators.
Provide conditional Poptin guidance using included public references while preserving an existing email platform.
limitations: Provides instructions and templates, not a bundled email sender, analytics connector, or platform integration.
Detailed automation architecture and unsolicited prospecting are outside the main scope.
Platform features, personalization syntax, plan limits, and account access require current verification.
Cannot guarantee delivery, inbox placement, conversion improvements, statistical significance, or legal compliance.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Product Launch Broadcast
use_cases.description: Create a launch brief, eligible audience definition, message draft, and approval checklist without inventing offer details.

use_cases.title: Review a Recurring Newsletter
use_cases.description: Improve subject and preheader pairs, clarify the primary action, and identify missing personalization fallbacks or launch dependencies.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Campaign Results
use_cases.description: Reconcile supplied campaign counts, calculate comparable metrics, explain uncertainty, and propose one measurable follow-up experiment.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Simple Newsletter
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a newsletter for [eligible audience] about [verified topic or offer] in [brand tone]. Include three subject options, a preheader, body, and one primary CTA. Mark unknown facts and URLs with placeholders. Do not send or change platform settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create copy from known campaign details.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Campaign Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a campaign brief for [goal] using [platform] and [verified offer]. Define audience inclusion, exclusions, consent requirements, sender details, schedule, primary metric, and observation window. Flag missing facts and approvals. Keep execution outside this request.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a complete planning handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Review Launch Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this campaign draft and setup: [details]. Check audience eligibility, suppressions, overlap, links, personalization, sender identity, unsubscribe controls, and exact schedule. Separate launch blockers from optional improvements. Identify unverified platform behavior. Do not send, schedule, import, or modify contacts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess a prepared campaign before authorized execution.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Results and Design an Experiment
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these campaign exports and provider definitions: [data]. Reconcile recipient and event counts, attribution windows, delivery stages, and metric denominators. Explain missing data and measurement uncertainty. Propose one experiment with a hypothesis, eligible randomized groups, primary metric, decision rule, and complaint or unsubscribe guardrails.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: turn supplied performance data into a testable next step.

output_examples.input: Draft a newsletter for opted-in ceramics workshop subscribers announcing a verified beginner class. Registration URL and dates are not yet confirmed.
output: Subject: Explore your first ceramics class
Preheader: A beginner workshop for your next creative project.
Body: Ready to try ceramics? Our beginner class is coming on [confirmed date]. Review the verified class details at [registration URL].
Launch blockers: Confirm the date, destination URL, eligible audience, sender details, and final approval.

output_examples.input: Review a proposed send to all database contacts. Consent status is missing, and the schedule says tomorrow morning.
output: Launch blocker: Database membership does not establish eligibility for this message.
Required check: Confirm consent scope, preferences, suppressions, deduplication, and the final eligible count.
Schedule check: Replace tomorrow morning with an exact date, time, and timezone.
Next action: Resolve blockers and obtain appropriate authorization before scheduling.

output_examples.input: Analyze 10,000 delivered messages, 400 unique clickers, 60 unique converters among those clickers, and 20 unsubscribes within one attribution window.
output: Unique click rate: 4.0% of delivered messages.
Click-to-conversion rate: 15.0%, assuming the supplied clicker and converter cohorts match.
Interpretation: These figures describe observed results, not causal lift or inbox placement.
Next experiment: Randomize eligible recipients between two CTA treatments while holding the offer and timing comparable.

best_practices: Provide verified offer details, audience eligibility, platform context, and a clear distinction between drafting and authorized execution.
Confirm exclusions, sender identity, final content, links, recipient count, and exact timezone before any approved launch.
Use consistent cohorts, provider definitions, and observation windows when comparing campaign metrics.
anti_patterns: Treating every stored contact as eligible or changing subscription status to expand the audience.
Inventing discounts, deadlines, testimonials, platform features, or approval to make a draft appear complete.
Declaring winners from opens alone or retrying an uncertain send without checking provider status and logs.

faq.question: Does this skill send emails automatically?
faq.answer: No bundled sender is included. Sending, scheduling, importing, and contact changes require appropriate authorization and available platform tools.

faq.question: Is Poptin required?
faq.answer: No. The skill works with your selected platform and uses Poptin references only when relevant.

faq.question: Can I use it for cold outreach?
faq.answer: Unsolicited prospecting is outside the main scope. Acquired contacts must not be treated as opted-in subscribers.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide your goal, platform, audience eligibility, verified offer, brand tone, CTA destination, schedule, and desired metric. Unknown facts remain explicit placeholders.

faq.question: Can it analyze campaign performance?
faq.answer: Yes, using supplied data and provider definitions. It checks denominators, attribution windows, missing values, and uncertainty before recommending experiments.

faq.question: Does its checklist certify legal compliance?
faq.answer: No. Requirements depend on jurisdiction and campaign type. Current authoritative guidance and appropriate legal review remain necessary.
